answer.rationale: Latency began climbing ~30 minutes after the release went out, which points to a regression in the new build rather than pure peak load; rollback is the most direct lever and b1 shows it previously cleared a similar error spike without customer impact, while b6 shows the gating infrastructure is trusted. Rolling back restores the known-stable build without losing in-flight writes (writes still commit; they are just slow), unlike failover which risks write divergence during peak settlement. Verified b1 and b2 to confirm rollback safety and to check whether regional failover behaved as cleanly as the consolidated memory claims before ruling it out. Uncertainty remains: if the release is unrelated and the cause is peak write contention, rollback will not help and add_capacity would be the next-window action.
